answer.answer: Volatility is how much an investment's value tends to swing up and down, usually measured over a year. When volatility is high, the value can rise or fall a lot in a short time. When it is low, the path is smoother. It shows how bumpy the ride is, not whether you end up gaining or losing. A more volatile portfolio can feel harder to stay with during sharp drops, so it's worth comparing it with how much loss you're comfortable seeing.
